outcomes: Callers choose a positive concurrency cap or an explicitly unbounded non-positive limit
Successful map results retain input order regardless of completion order
The first worker failure cancels siblings, stops bounded dispatch when cancellation is observed, and skips unbounded user work when cancellation is visible before invocation
A worker panic is returned as structured error data instead of terminating the process
nonGoals: Returning partial results after any worker fails
Guaranteeing worker start order or scheduling fairness
Forcibly terminating a worker that ignores context cancellation

requirements.text: A positive limit bounds in-flight workers, while a non-positive limit permits one goroutine per item.

Bounded dispatch stays within its throughput budget: mapping a trivial worker over a large batch sustains at least 50 000 items per second. The budget is an order-of-magnitude tripwire with roughly thirty times headroom over the measured rate, not a service objective — it catches a structural regression in the dispatch path, never runner noise.

The first worker error wins atomically, cancels the shared child context, and suppresses partial results. With a positive limit, the dispatcher stops launching workers when cancellation is observed; with a non-positive limit, an already-created goroutine skips the user function when cancellation is visible before invocation.
MapBounded stores each successful result at its input index and returns the complete ordered slice only when every worker succeeds.
A recovered worker panic returns PanicError with the recovered value and worker stack and participates in normal first-error cancellation.
